wasm-html-to-image merges an HTML layout/rendering pipeline and an image optimization/encoding pipeline into a single native WebAssembly binary. Traditional setups require two separate libraries: one rendering HTML to PNG, and another re-encoding PNG to WebP or AVIF. This causes substantial memory allocations and data copying across JavaScript boundaries. wasm-html-to-image eliminates this overhead by piping the rendered Bitmap directly to the encoder within the single Skia-WASM module.

Resource Discovery (satoru_collect_resources): Parses image URLs, @font-face rules, and CSS backgrounds from HTML/CSS. Resource Injection (satoru_add_resource): TypeScript fetches needed resources concurrently using in-memory process caches. Layout & Painting: litehtml computes the box layout, HarfBuzz/SkUnicode shapes text, and Skia renders to an off-screen surface. Output Generation: svg / pdf: Skia streams vector commands directly. Raster formats: Rendered Bitmap is piped straight to native encoders without leaving WASM linear memory.

When given image buffers or data URLs: Direct Decoding: Bypasses the HTML layout engine completely. Transformations: Applies width, height, fit, and crop directly in the image pipeline. Encoding: Compresses to WebP, AVIF, JXL, JPEG, RAW pixels, or ThumbHash.

The repeat count is set with loop (CLI: --animation-loop) and defaults to 0 (infinite).

Box Model: Margins, paddings, borders, box-sizing (border-box, content-box), aspect-ratio, and logical properties (margin-inline, padding-block, etc.). Flexbox: Multi-pass resolution conforming to W3C Flexbox specs (flex-direction, justify-content, align-items, flex-wrap, gap, row-gap, column-gap, etc.). Grid Layout: Grid tracks (grid-template-columns/rows), item placement (grid-column/row), implicit tracks (grid-auto-columns/rows), grid-auto-flow (row, column, and dense hole filling), place-items, gap. Typography & Internationalization: HarfBuzz text shaping, bidirectional text (BiDi), unicode-bidi (bidi-override / isolate-override map to line-item order; embed / isolate boundaries and per-run glyph reversal are partial), line-breaking for CJK, Latin, Arabic, and Emoji. Vertical text (writing-mode: vertical-rl), multi-line truncation (-webkit-line-clamp / max-lines + block-ellipsis / text-overflow: ellipsis), text-transform, and text stroke (-webkit-text-stroke). Fonts for scripts missing from Noto Sans JP (Hangul, Hebrew, Arabic, Thai, Devanagari, Greek) and for color emoji are fetched on demand from external CDNs (Google Fonts / jsDelivr) only when such characters appear. Font Features: font-feature-settings, font-variant-* (-ligatures, -numeric, -east-asian, -caps, -position), font-kerning, font-variation-settings, font-stretch. OpenType features (palt, kern, liga, pnum, zero, …) are applied through HarfBuzz per element; variable axes (wght, wdth, …) and stretch keywords/percentages are supported. Synthetic small-caps, synthetic sub/super, @font-face stretch descriptors, and optical sizing are partial or unsupported. Text Decoration: text-decoration (-line, -style, -color, -thickness), text-decoration-skip-ink, text-underline-position, text-underline-offset. Solid, dashed, dotted, double, and wavy underlines, overlines, and line-throughs; skip-ink splits the line around glyph ink and also applies to vertical writing. Percentages for thickness and underline-offset resolve against the element's font size. Visual Effects: Box shadows (multiple shadows, inset), border-radii (elliptical, individual corners), box-decoration-break: clone (PDF page fragments of block boxes get complete borders, corners and background; inline line breaks are unaffected), corner-shape (round / scoop / bevel / notch / squircle / square / superellipse() plus per-corner longhands; applied to backgrounds, borders, box-shadow and clipping), transforms, opacity, filters (blur, drop-shadow), backdrop filters, blend modes (mix-blend-mode, background-blend-mode), and image-rendering (pixelated uses nearest-neighbour sampling for and background images, including tiles; crisp-edges is unsupported). Motion Path: offset-path (ray(), path(), basic shapes), offset-distance, offset-rotate, offset-anchor, offset-position, and the offset shorthand. Position and tangent rotation along the path are supported with Chromium-checked grammar (lengths including calc(), coordinate boxes). url() references and strict handling are unsupported. Clipping & Shapes: Native Skia vector clipping paths (circle(), ellipse(), polygon(), path(), inset()), and alpha masks (mask, mask-image, mask-size, mask-repeat, mask-position; images and gradients, tiled). Inline SVG: Direct embedded

wasm-html-to-image is a lightweight static renderer based on litehtml and Skia, not a headless browser. Keep the following constraints in mind when writing templates: NO JavaScript: <script> tags, DOM event listeners, and DOM APIs do not run. Partial CSS Animation Support: transition is not evaluated. @keyframes are ignored by default (only static styles paint), but passing animation: { duration, fps, loop } (CLI: --animation) samples opacity, transform and color / background-color @keyframes into an animated WebP / APNG / GIF. The repeat count is set with loop (CLI: --animation-loop, default 0 = infinite). Defaults are 15 fps with caps of 5 s (duration is clamped to 5000 ms) / ~75 frames. The CSS animation-duration (including the animation shorthand, var() supported) is the length of one iteration; together with animation-delay and animation-iteration-count (a number or infinite) it defines the sampled timeline (infinite samples one iteration, alternate / alternate-reverse two). The API duration is an upper bound on the whole timeline and the API fps caps the frame rate. transform supports translate / rotate / scale only; when the function list differs between the keyframes the element keeps its static transform. An animation-timing-function inside a keyframe block applies to the interval that starts at that stop, and the element-level one (<style> or inline) is the default (linear / ease / ease-in / ease-out / ease-in-out / cubic-bezier() / steps() / step-start / step-end; applied to opacity, color and transform interpolation). animation-direction (normal / reverse / alternate / alternate-reverse) and animation-fill-mode (none / forwards / backwards / both) are honoured, so the value during animation-delay (backwards) and after the animation (forwards) is resolved; a negative animation-delay starts inside the first iteration. Every @keyframes block of the document animates all the elements its rule selects (several allowed); several animations on one element (animation-name: a, b) remain out of scope. NO Canvas Scripting: <canvas> element 2D/WebGL contexts do not execute. Use inline <svg> or CSS shapes instead. NO Interactive States: :hover, :active, and :focus states do not trigger. NO Browser Web Storage: window, document, localStorage, and IndexedDB are unavailable.

Node.js (>=20): Full support across single, multi-threaded worker pools, and explicit modules. Cloudflare Workers: Full support via wasm-html-to-image/workerd. Vercel Edge Runtime: Full support via wasm-html-to-image/edge-light. Browsers: Runs client-side or within Web Workers. Deno & Bun: Fully compatible.

wasm-html-to-image is an ultra-fast, self-contained HTML-to-image and image conversion engine that consolidates an HTML rendering engine (Satoru) and an image optimization engine (wasm-image-optimization) into a single WebAssembly (Emscripten) module. It requires no heavy headless browsers like Chromium, Puppeteer, or Playwright, and runs portably across server-side runtimes, edge environments such as Cloudflare Workers, browsers, and the CLI.

Single Unified WASM Module: Parses HTML, calculates CSS layout, renders with Skia, and encodes images (WebP/AVIF/JPEG, etc.) inside one binary without passing intermediate frame buffers across JS boundaries. Versatile Inputs: Supports HTML strings, HTML string arrays (for multi-page PDF), URLs, and raw image buffers (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, AVIF, BMP, Data URLs). Multiple Output Formats: Direct SVG vector output, high-quality PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF, raw pixels, ThumbHash, and multi-page PDF generation. Zero-Config render(): Import directly from wasm-html-to-image and render immediately without manual WASM loading or setup (automatically resolves workerd in Cloudflare Workers). Edge & Cloudflare Workers Ready: Along with auto-detection, dedicated wasm-html-to-image/workerd and edge-light subpaths fit constrained serverless edge environments. Parallel Worker Pool: Built-in multi-threaded pool in wasm-html-to-image/workers allows batch generation without stalling the main event loop. Rich Ecosystem Integration: Seamless JSX rendering for React and Preact, plus UnoCSS-based Tailwind CSS utility classes.

In addition to HTML rendering, wasm-html-to-image functions as a high-speed, native image conversion, resizing, and optimization engine.

Automatic Format Detection (isImageInput): Recognizes magic bytes for PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, AVIF, BMP, or data:image/... strings. Zero Overhead: Bypasses the HTML/CSS DOM layout phase completely, routing directly from Skia's native decoders into the image encoding pipeline. Comprehensive Output Features: Modern Next-Gen Compression: Convert large PNGs/JPEGs into compact WebP or AVIF files. Resize & Fit: Supports width, height, fit (contain / cover / fill), and crop. Vector SVG Generation: Wraps image data directly inside an SVG document. Single-page PDF Generation: Wraps image into a 1-page vector PDF. ThumbHash Generation: Generates ultra-compact placeholder blur hashes directly.

wasm-html-to-image functions not only as an HTML renderer but also as a high-performance native engine for image format conversion, resizing, compression, and ThumbHash generation. You can handle common image transformation tasks without pulling in heavy native dependencies like Sharp or ImageMagick.

Input image buffers (Uint8Array or Buffer) are automatically detected via magic bytes: Input Format (Auto-detected) Available Output Formats PNG webp, avif, jxl, jpeg, png, raw, thumbhash, svg, pdf JPEG webp, avif, jxl, jpeg, png, raw, thumbhash, svg, pdf WebP avif, jxl, webp, jpeg, png, raw, thumbhash, svg, pdf GIF (including animated) webp (with animation), png, jpeg, avif, jxl, etc. AVIF webp, jxl, jpeg, png, raw, thumbhash, svg, pdf BMP webp, avif, jxl, jpeg, png, raw, thumbhash, svg, pdf

import fs from "node:fs/promises"; import { render } from "wasm-html-to-image/single"; const inputImage = await fs.readFile("photo.jpg"); // Convert JPEG -> WebP (quality: 80) const webp = await render({ value: inputImage, width: 800, format: "webp", quality: 80, fit: "contain", }); await fs.writeFile("photo.webp", Buffer.from(webp)); // Convert JPEG -> AVIF (highest compression) const avif = await render({ value: inputImage, width: 800, format: "avif", quality: 75, speed: 6, // 0 (slowest, best quality) to 10 (fastest) }); await fs.writeFile("photo.avif", Buffer.from(avif));
documents.s: A. Convert JPEG/PNG to WebP / AVIF

documents.t: // Crop a 400x400 area starting from (100, 100), then scale down to 200x200 const cropped = await render({ value: inputImage, crop: { x: 100, y: 100, width: 400, height: 400 }, width: 200, height: 200, format: "png", });

Set animation: true to preserve all frames in the output: const gifData = await fs.readFile("animation.gif"); const animatedWebp = await render({ value: gifData, format: "webp", quality: 75, animation: true, }); await fs.writeFile("animation.webp", Buffer.from(animatedWebp));

Dynamically serve images directly from Next.js App Router handlers (app/api/og/route.ts). // app/api/og/route.ts import { NextRequest } from "next/server"; import { render } from "wasm-html-to-image/single"; export async function GET(req: NextRequest) { const { searchParams } = new URL(req.url); const title = searchParams.get("title") || "Next.js Blog"; const png = await render({ value: `

${title}

`, width: 1200, height: 630, format: "png", }); return new Response(png, { headers: { "Content-Type": "image/png", "Cache-Control": "public, max-age=31536000, immutable", }, }); }

Building an automated Open Graph Image generator with custom HTML/CSS layouts. import { Hono } from "hono"; import { render } from "wasm-html-to-image/single"; const app = new Hono(); app.get("/ogp", async (c) => { const title = c.req.query("title") || "No Title"; const html = `

${title}

`; const image = await render({ value: html, width: 1200, height: 630, format: "png", }); return new Response(image, { headers: { "Content-Type": "image/png", "Cache-Control": "public, max-age=86400", }, }); }); export default app;

Generate multi-page vector PDF documents by supplying an array of HTML strings (string[]). import fs from "node:fs/promises"; import { render } from "wasm-html-to-image/single"; const pages = [ `

Monthly Summary

Page 1 Overview

`, `

Detailed Statistics

Page 2 Content

`, ]; const pdf = await render({ value: pages, width: 595, // A4 width (pt) height: 842, // A4 height (pt) format: "pdf", mediaType: "print", pdfTitle: "Report 2026", }); await fs.writeFile("report.pdf", Buffer.from(pdf));

Mass generation of hundreds or thousands of banners using multi-core worker threads. import fs from "node:fs/promises"; import path from "node:path"; import { render } from "wasm-html-to-image/workers"; const items = Array.from({ length: 50 }, (_, i) => ({ id: `card-${i + 1}`, title: `Item #${i + 1}`, })); async function runBatch() { await Promise.all( items.map(async (item) => { const webp = await render({ value: `

${item.title}

`, width: 600, height: 400, format: "webp", }); await fs.writeFile(`./dist/${item.id}.webp`, Buffer.from(webp)); }), ); } runBatch();
